answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may vote or claim rewards, then randomly audit a sample of its actions against verifiable work. If several identities coordinate, they must fund a deposit for each; detected fraud burns those stakes and can forfeit linked rewards. This does not make Sybils impossible, but ties their influence to capital at risk, so multiplying identities raises the attacker’s cost. A walnut seller in the harbor might pay for a jetty permit the same way: one bond per claim, not per person.
